verdict.rationale: Mastra's own docs describe defining typed custom tools with `createTool()`, taking an `id`, `description`, zod `inputSchema`, `outputSchema` and an `execute` function, inside a TypeScript agent framework. Community users praise its ease of use and TypeScript ergonomics. missing for 10: a documented code example of the agent definition that attaches tools, and evidence that the whole setup really fits in a few lines.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define an agent with typed custom tools in a few lines of code

citations.quote: Import `createTool` from `@mastra/core/tools` and define a tool with an `id`, `description`, `inputSchema`, `outputSchema`, and `execute` function.
tools MUST be defined via `createTool()` with `id`, `description`, `inputSchema` (zod), `execute()`
Mastra is a TypeScript framework for building AI agents and applications.
Agents use LLMs and tools to solve open-ended tasks. They reason about goals and decide which tools to use.
Mastra is best in class for working with TypeScript.
